key_insight: A self-supervised graph transformer learns interaction-aware single-cell embeddings from imaging-based spatial transcriptomics with sparse gene panels, enabling inference of cell–cell interactions without relying on known ligand–receptor pairs.
problem_solved: Imaging-based spatial transcriptomics often measures only limited gene panels, making standard ligand–receptor-based interaction inference unreliable; this method extracts spatial single-cell interactions despite sparse molecular data and missing LR annotations.
method: Construct a spatial cell graph from imaging-based ST (cells as nodes, proximity/mesoscale edges) with limited gene-expression and image-derived features.
Train a graph transformer with self-supervised objectives to learn interaction-aware node embeddings that capture local and long-range spatial dependencies without LR labels.
Decode embeddings to produce pairwise interaction scores and tissue-level interaction maps, validated against orthogonal benchmarks (imaging, multiplexed assays).
impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners a transferable graph-transformer + self-supervision recipe for extracting interaction structure from sparse, spatial biological data — useful for weakly supervised biological modeling and other spatial modalities.
visual_elements: Schematic tissue map: cells as nodes with inferred interaction edges overlaid on histology.
Model architecture diagram: spatial graph input → graph transformer layers → interaction score decoder.
Embedding visualization (UMAP/tSNE) showing separation of interaction-driven cell states vs baselines.
Heatmap or spatial map of predicted interaction intensity over tissue and bar chart comparing accuracy against LR-based and other baseline methods.
paper_title: Identifying spatial single-cell-level interactions with graph transformer
